sources.title: How Claude remembers your project
findings: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md as the always-loaded project instruction surface.
If a repository already uses AGENTS.md for other agents, CLAUDE.md should import AGENTS.md to avoid duplication rather than restating it.
If an entry is a multi-step procedure or only matters for part of the codebase, it belongs in a skill or path-scoped rule instead of broad CLAUDE.md memory.
Auto memory is a Claude-written recall surface, not the human-authored instruction source.

sources.title: Best Practices for Claude Code
findings: Claude performs better when exploration, planning, and implementation are separated.
CLAUDE.md should stay short, human-readable, and broadly applicable; workflows or occasionally relevant domain knowledge should move into skills.
Subagents are recommended for investigation to preserve main-thread context quality.
Explicit verification and success criteria are a high-leverage ingredient for agentic coding quality.

sources.title: Extend Claude with skills
findings: Skills are the right home for reusable workflows, large procedures, and progressively disclosed reference content.
Anthropic explicitly recommends creating a skill when a section of CLAUDE.md has grown into a procedure rather than a fact.

sources.title: Hooks reference
findings: PreToolUse hooks are the hard-control layer for allow, deny, ask, defer, and tool-input modification decisions.
Hooks can tighten behavior but remain bounded by broader permission precedence.

sources.title: Custom instructions with AGENTS.md
findings: Codex reads AGENTS.md before work and layers global guidance with project-specific overrides.
Instruction discovery is size-bounded by project_doc_max_bytes (32 KiB by default), which argues against turning always-on instruction files into research banks.
Nested overrides should sit close to specialized work rather than bloating the root guidance layer.
Alternate always-on filenames are ignored unless explicitly configured as fallback filenames.

sources.title: Agent Skills
findings: Skills are the authoring format for reusable workflows in Codex.
Codex begins with skill metadata and loads the full skill body only when the skill is selected, which makes skills a better fit than always-on instruction files for evolving or procedural guidance.

sources.title: Memories
findings: Memories are a local recall layer for stable preferences and recurring workflows rather than the authoritative rule surface.
Required team guidance should remain in AGENTS.md or checked-in documentation.

sources.title: Rules
findings: Execution control belongs in Codex rules rather than in always-on instruction prose.

sources.title: Agent approvals & security
findings: Approval behavior lives in sandbox and approval configuration rather than in always-on instruction text.

repo_findings: The current repo already encodes strong overlap with the four Karpathy principles across CLAUDE.md, orchestrator guidance, builder posture, context-map, and the Trust Contract.

T-KRP-A should add a named operating lens, not a second canonical policy layer, because CLAUDE.md already centralizes development rules and AGENTS.md is generated output rather than a human-authored instruction source.
For this slice, root CLAUDE.md is the sole human-authored placement surface; AGENTS.md and any other mirrors are generated consequences or explicit non-goals unless a later slice says otherwise.

Anthropic's CLAUDE.md guidance and OpenAI's AGENTS.md guidance do not conflict once mapped onto Azoth's current repo architecture: CLAUDE.md is the T-KRP-A authoring target, while AGENTS.md parity remains generated or deferred.

The thin-layer shape for T-KRP-A should preserve the split of later follow-ons: T-KRP-C for deeper builder hardening, T-KRP-D for orchestrator assumption-surfacing, and T-KRP-E for goal-to-success-criteria gating.
The task-scoped reusable artifact should live under .azoth/research/, while SWARM_RESEARCH_DIGEST.yaml remains a roadmap-level swarm aggregate rather than the per-slice bank entry.

Current exploratory write access is intentionally narrow and exact-path only. Safe research-bank persistence in general exploratory sessions needs a separate exploratory-artifact class or session-bound write policy rather than a wider raw allowlist.
